The script creates a default `config.toml` if one does not exist, setting paths for saves and disabling auto-updates—consistent with the comment explaining that updates are managed via `pacman`, not the application. It sets `HALO_UPDATE_AUTO=false` in the environment to enforce this. All operations are confined to user-writable directories and the predefined system directory `/usr/lib/opence`. There are no network operations, no execution of downloaded code, no obfuscation, and no attempts to escalate privileges or exfiltrate data.

The behavior aligns with standard AUR packaging practices for games that require mutable per-user copies of binaries or configs. While the use of `exec` with a copied binary may seem unusual, it is not inherently malicious—especially in the context of games that may not support running from system directories directly. No evidence of supply-chain attack or injected malicious code is present.
